name: Pixeldrain
aliases: ipfs / arweave / filecoin pinning as the hidden upstream

card.summary: Free plan: storage 'No limit' for regular uploads (2 TB limit only on the paid filesystem product). Pro: no limit; Prepaid: EUR 4/TB/month metered.

free_tier.stated: Free plan: storage 'No limit' for regular uploads (2 TB limit only on the paid filesystem product). Pro: no limit; Prepaid: EUR 4/TB/month metered.

retention.stated: Files expire 60 days after last download; a download only counts if >10% of the file was transferred in one request, and the timer only updates once per 24h

egress.terms: Free egress capped at 6 GB/day per IP address (sliding 24h window, IP-bound even when logged in); over the cap the speed drops to 1 MiB/s and max 3 concurrent downloads. Pro: 4 TB per 30 days. Prepaid: EUR 1/TB metered. So free egress is metered, not unusable. 6 GB/day x N IPs.

record.tooling: Full REST API at /api with HTTP Basic (api key as password). rclone has no official backend; the API is simple enough that wrappers abound (Atlas electron/downloads/hosts/pixeldrain.js). PUT https://pixeldrain.com/api/file/ with -u :APIKEY.
record.chaining: API keys are free and per-account, but the real multiplier is IP: the 6 GB/day download cap is per IP, so egress scales with egress IPs (proxies/CF Workers) not accounts. Storage itself is 'No limit' on free, which is the interesting half.
record.limits_note: Free uploads require an API key (anonymous server-side PUT returned 401 authentication_required). 6 GB/day/IP download cap; 1 MiB/s throttle and 3 concurrent downloads after that. Files expire 60 days after last download; a download only counts if >10% of the file was transferred in one request, and the timer only updates once per 24h. Hotlinking not supported on free.
record.reliability_note: Operator states plainly that free-plan 'unlimited' is not for storage: 'If you are (ab)using pixeldrain for free storage, you should not be surprised when the rules change at some point and all your stuff suddenly disappears.' The 6 GB/day free cap and 10%-of-file rule make this a poor serving tier unless fronted by something that fans out across IPs.

evidence.proved: pricing table: Free 'Storage: No limit'; 'Egress transfer limit - 6 GB per day ... linked to your IP address'; 'When the download limit is exceeded the download speed is reduced to 1 MiB/s. You can have at most three concurrent downloads'
'Files will be removed if they have not been accessed for 60 days ... This only happens when someone downloads more than 10% of the whole file in a single request'
'All methods which create, modify or delete a resource require an API key'; base URL /api, Basic auth

record.notes: Free plan: storage 'No limit' for regular uploads (2 TB limit only on the paid filesystem product). Pro: no limit; Prepaid: EUR 4/TB/month metered.
record.binding_note: a clock, not a quota: bytes leave whether or not transfer is completed
